subject: Banking
title: The Revolving Door of Banking Profit
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Revolving Door of Banking Profit.

hook.text: Banks earned record profits in 2023 while customers faced rising fees, higher loan rates, and low savings yields.

buildup.text: Every product banks sell transfers wealth from customers to shareholders: interest spreads, fees, trading.

discovery.text: The banking profit model is circular: deposits fund loans, loans generate interest.

twist.text: Government guarantees lower the cost of risk. Banks keep the profits in good years and pass losses to taxpayers in bad.

climax.text: Banking's profit engine never stops because it's powered by everyday economic activity.

punchline.text: Every transaction feeds the bank. Banking profits from all economic activity.

quiz.question: What makes banking profits so persistent?
options: Banks profit from essentially all economic activity flowing through them

details.summary: Banks profit from employees who move between banking and government regulatory roles, gaining insider knowledge of regulations and building relationships. This revolving door shapes the rules that determine how banks make money.
details.whyItMatters: The revolving door creates an inherent conflict where regulators may soften rules knowing they want future bank employment, and ex-regulators help banks navigate rules they once wrote. It shapes the environment bank profits depend on.
takeaways: Former regulators command premium salaries at banks they once oversaw
Banks hire former regulators for their knowledge of enforcement patterns
Cooling-off periods attempt to limit the revolving door but are often short

faq.question: How does the revolving door benefit banks?
faq.answer: Former regulators bring deep knowledge of how their agencies think, what triggers enforcement, and personal relationships with current officials. This inside information helps banks structure activities to maximize profit while staying just within regulatory boundaries.

faq.question: What is regulatory capture?
faq.answer: Regulatory capture occurs when regulators begin serving the interests of the industries they oversee rather than the public. The revolving door contributes to this by creating personal financial incentives for regulators to maintain friendly relationships with banks.
